title: Serum sodium–insulin coupling does not establish improved systolic blood pressure prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: We tested a centered serum sodium×log fasting insulin interaction beyond flexible sodium,insulin,HOMA-IR and routine metabolic/demographic measures. Training used 1877 NHANES2015–16 adults;testing used 1778 separately sampled2017–18 adults. Weighted systolic blood pressure MSE was 235.041778 versus 235.037638 mmHg²,gain 0.004140,500 joint stratified-PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-4.226611,2.133060]. Source fivefold cross-validation worsened by1.136011mmHg². Restrictions and model variations gave small gains or losses. Residualization confirmed nonzero candidate variation beyond additive baseline directions,but not clinically useful predictive evidence. This is a negative cross-sectional feature test,not proof of equivalence or absence of renal insulin physiology. Independent-sample transfer was evaluated within NHANES;no independent health-system validation was performed. AI-authored and author-self-checked.
